SPEC COMPLIANCE CHUNK FP-06: FHIRPath — §5.5.1 iif, §5.5.2 Boolean Conversion, §5.5.3 Integer Conversion. Test these items: iif(criterion, true-result, otherwise-result), toBoolean(), convertsToBoolean(), toInteger(), convertsToInteger(). For DuckDB-backed FHIRPath/CQL surfaces, test both the native/C++ extension path and the Python fallback where both exist, and compare outputs between paths. For SQL-on-FHIR ViewDefinition chunks, test parser validation, SQL generation, DuckDB execution, and official spec fixtures/examples relevant to the chunk.

When the pipeline is fully complete, set workflow to null, set exit_reason, write all handoff files, and return control to the outer spec compliance orchestrator.

issues.spec_citation: FHIRPath Normative Release §5.5.2 convertsToBoolean() and §5.5.3 convertsToInteger(); §5.5 states conversion functions operate on single-item input collections and these signatures take no arguments.
issues.evidence: Both native C++ and forced Python fallback return fhirpath_is_valid=true and concrete results for invalid argument-bearing calls: 'true'.convertsToBoolean(2) => ['false']; '1'.convertsToInteger(2) => ['true']; convertsToBoolean(strTrue) => ['true']; convertsToInteger(strInt) => ['true']. Expected public row resilience is empty/NULL with fhirpath_is_valid=false because these conversion functions have zero-argument signatures.
issues.root_cause: The Python invocation registry advertised a non-spec one-argument convenience form for convertsToBoolean/convertsToInteger, and the native evaluator did not enforce zero-argument arity before dispatching those functions.
issues.resolution: Restricted Python convertsToBoolean/convertsToInteger arity to zero arguments and added matching native C++ arity checks. Added native/fallback parity tests and native sqllogictest coverage for invalid argument-bearing forms.
